title: fix(ui): preserve boot cache deadlines during Gateway updates
body:
Related: #189738

## What Problem This Solves

Unrelated Gateway updates can keep postponing the Control UI's pending boot-cache write, leaving reload recovery without the latest sidebar catalog.

## User Impact

Navigation, canvas-lease updates, and session-row activity no longer restart an unchanged boot record's write deadline. Actual catalog, identity, connection, and readiness changes still update the cache.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing deadline protection only filtered session notifications. Gateway and agent notifications still reset the same timer. Compare the boot-record inputs at their shared persistence owner so every subscriber follows the same rule; retain the existing debounce for changed data.

## Evidence

- Scheduled run [41269343462](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41269343462), `checks-ui (2/3)`, failed the boot-record deadline case.
- The existing regression now publishes an unrelated Gateway update at 400ms and still requires the original write at 500ms. It fails on the unchanged implementation and passes with this fix.
- Focused Bun proof: 47 tests passed across boot-record and warm-boot recovery suites; original assertions remain intact.
- The same Bun deadline case passed 31 consecutive executions after the fix.
- UI typecheck (tsrs), targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Local autoreview through P2 covered the final two-file diff against `c2a39e4c5a8`: complete and clean, no findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; hosted ClawSweeper review is queued.

The change adds no storage format, timers, or cache owner. UI appearance is unchanged.

### PR CI follow-up

Run 41271534408 is red on unrelated baseline UI failures: shards 1 and 3 import Node-only `node:util/types.isProxy` through core transcript ownership code, then fail to mount chat/sidebar panels; shard 2 reports an unhandled Vitest browser mock-factory rejection without a named failed case. These browser sources, fixtures, configuration, and dependency inputs are unchanged by this PR. A baseline replay reproduces the Node import failure. The three active shard-2 browser files pass 71/71 on both baseline and PR head; the original mock transport trigger remains uncertain. The scoped boot-cache regression remains green. These failures are being retained as failures and attributed for the authorized inherited-CI landing route.
